events.objective: Establish the true onset timeline and blast radius for INC-012. For the window 2026-06-01T14:00Z to 16:59Z, query logs and metrics to determine: (1) the exact minute payment-service error rate departed from baseline, and whether it matches the ~15-min-after-v6.0.0 timeline the reporter claims; (2) the exact error signature(s) on payment-service (are they ledger-write errors, timeouts, auth failures, or app exceptions?); (3) which OTHER services (especially ledger-service, any database, queue, or shared dependency named in payment-service logs/metrics) show degradation, and whether they degraded BEFORE or AFTER payment-service; (4) whether ledger-service's own write failures are internal errors or downstream dependency failures. Report per-service onset times and the dominant error strings.

Determine what changed around 2026-06-01T14:45-15:10Z across ALL services, not just payment-service. Pull deploy history (especially payment-service v6.0.0 and anything in ledger-service or shared components), config/feature-flag changes, and service dependency topology (what payment-service depends on, what depends on ledger-service, any shared DB/schema/queue). Also search historical incidents for prior 'new ledger entry type' / ledger-write-failure events and their root causes and fixes.

Correlate changes against onset: using the precise onset time and blast-radius ordering found in task a, identify which change (deploy, config, or flag) is the earliest change preceding that onset and best explains the affected service set — and explicitly test whether payment-service v6.0.0 is the root cause or merely the trigger that exposed a downstream ledger-service/schema incompatibility. Assess why the v6.0.0 mandate flow's new ledger entry type could fail writes (unknown entry type rejected by ledger schema, enum mismatch, missing DB migration, capacity), and whether anything else new was introduced in the same window.

events.statement: Exactly one deployment occurred anywhere in the 13:30-15:30Z window: dep-6203, payment-service v6.0.0 (author p.nair, 'New UPI mandate flow'), deployed_at 2026-06-01T14:46:00Z, changes include 'new ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD', status 'rolled_back' at 2026-06-01T15:12:00Z.

No config or feature-flag changes were recorded for any service in 13:30-15:30Z (count 0, scope 'all services'); a per-service query for payment-service over 2026-05-31T00:00Z-16:59Z also returned count 0. Change surface in the incident window is deploy-only.
payment-service depends on ledger-db via a db edge, on bank-partner-api (external, no telemetry), and produces to kafka; api-gateway calls payment-service over http.

ledger-db is a SHARED postgres (owner platform) with four writer services: order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service all have 'kind':'db' edges to it — a neighbour can affect payment-service through this shared datastore.

There is no service named 'ledger-service' in the topology/release system; the only ledger component is the shared datastore ledger-db (known_services include 'ledger-db' and no separate ledger-service). So no ledger-side application deploy could have happened.

Historical precedent: ledger-db has twice been the site of ledger-write problems — HIST-114 (2025-04-18) 'ledger-db disk full from retained WAL' with symptom 'write failures', root cause an inactive replication slot retaining WAL until disk filled; and HIST-111 (2025-05-22) new report query without an index causing full table scans/slow queries on ledger-db. No prior incident is titled or caused by a 'new ledger entry type', so the MANDATE_HOLD entry type has no recorded precedent.

No timeout, auth, or app-exception patterns dominate (only 2 GC WARNs, 2 connection-reset WARNs, 1 TLS WARN in the whole set).

ledger-db (the actual backing DB; there is no service named 'ledger-service') showed disk pressure BEFORE payment-service's errors: WARN 'disk usage 90% on /var/lib/postgresql/data' at 13:10:01Z, 95% at 14:15:45Z, and 98% at 14:48:20Z, plus repeated inactive replication-slot WAL retention warnings from 13:02:25Z. Hard write failures followed at 15:01:01Z.

ledger-db's failures are internal storage exhaustion, not downstream dependency failures: 153 PANICs 'could not write to file "pg_wal/xlogtemp.<n>": No space left on device' (first 15:01:01Z) and 139 'could not extend file "base/<n>/<n>": No space left on device' (first 15:01:39Z) — the DB itself ran out of disk for WAL and data files.

order-service shows the SAME storage error independently, not routed through payment: 236 occurrences of 'INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device', first_seen 2026-06-01T15:00:42Z — i.e. it began degrading in the same minute as payment-service, indicating a shared-storage blast radius rather than a payment-v6.0.0-specific bug.

Ordering of onsets: ledger-db disk-pressure WARNs (13:10Z onward) precede payment-service errors; ledger-db hard PANICs (15:01:01Z) are essentially simultaneous with, not after, payment-service's first error (15:00:26Z) and order-service's first error (15:00:42Z) — the consumers surfaced errors within the same minute the DB ran out of space.

events.answer: payment-service's error rate departed baseline in the 15:00Z bucket: it was flat at ~0.19-0.29% through the 14:56 bucket, then jumped to avg 60.15% at 15:00Z (tc-006). The first payment-service ERROR log is at 15:00:26Z, so the observed onset is ~15:00Z, NOT the reporter's "~15 minutes after v6.0.0" (which would put it ≈15:10Z, and the incident was only reported at 15:10). The dominant payment-service error signature is a ledger write failure carrying a storage error: "ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device" (354 occurrences from 15:00:26Z). The root signal is one level down: ledger-db logged rising disk pressure from 13:10Z (90% → 95% at 14:15Z → 98% at 14:48Z) and then crossed into hard failures at 15:01:01Z with "PANIC: could not write to file \"pg_wal/xlogtemp...\": No space left on device". Crucially, order-service shows the SAME storage error independently ("INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device", first at 15:00:42Z), so this is a shared-storage/blast-radius event, not specific to the payment v6.0.0 mandate flow. ledgers-db's own write failures are internal storage exhaustion (out of disk for WAL/data files), not a downstream dependency failure of ledger-db.

events.answer: The earliest (and only) change preceding the ~15:00Z onset is payment-service deploy dep-6203 (v6.0.0, 14:46Z, "new ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD", rolled back 15:12Z); no config/flag change and no ledger-db change exist. But it is NOT the root cause: the errors on payment-service are "No space left on device" storage failures from the SHARED ledger-db, which showed disk pressure from 13:10Z (before the 14:46Z deploy) and hard PANICs at 15:01:01Z. order-service hit the same error independently at 15:00:42Z, so the blast radius is shared-storage exhaustion, not a MANDATE_HOLD schema/enum incompatibility. v6.0.0 is at most a coincident trigger/contributor to write volume; the failure mode (unknown-entry-type rejection) is not present in the data, and the closest historical precedent (HIST-114) is a WAL-retention disk-full event.

events.title: Independent ledger-db storage exhaustion (inactive replication slot retaining WAL) fills the disk; all four writer services fail
payment-service v6.0.0 mandate flow's new MANDATE_HOLD write pattern amplified ledger-db pressure and triggered the disk exhaustion
v6.0.0's new MANDATE_HOLD entry type was rejected by ledger-db schema/enum (or a missing migration), producing ledger write failures
Rollback of payment-service is masking a still-broken shared datastore; the fault predates and outlives the deploy

events.summary: H1 (ledger-db storage exhaustion from retained WAL) is the only hypothesis consistent with the full evidence set. Temporal order is decisive: ledger-db's disk-pressure WARNs start 13:10Z and WAL-retention warnings at 13:02Z (F9) — ~1.5h BEFORE the only change in the window, payment-service v6.0.0 at 14:46Z (F1/F13) — and the consumers fail at 15:00:26Z/15:00:42Z. Scope is explained by the shared postgres: order-service (no change received, never writes MANDATE_HOLD) fails independently with the identical 'No space left on device' error (F11/F16), which a payment-code-path bug or an enum/type rejection (H3) cannot produce. Mechanism is grounded in ledger-db's own internal PANICs writing pg_wal and data files (F10), and the dominant client error (354x) is a storage error, not a type/constraint error (F8). H2 is properly demoted: its central hop (extra write volume from MANDATE_HOLD) has no supporting metric (automated check), and its timeline is impossible — the volume was already 90% at 13:10Z and only reached 98% at 14:48Z, far too slow a trajectory to be launched by a 14:46Z deploy, and F7 shows error rate stayed 59-64% well past the 15:12Z rollback. Accepted, with confidence capped below the stated 0.82 because the disk-fill trajectory is log-derived only (no independent ledger-db disk_used_pct metric) and the inactive-replication-slot mechanism is an inferred, unread assumption. Remaining open questions are confirmatory of an already-established origin, not discriminators between competing origins, so no further round is warranted.

events.why: top hypothesis is above threshold and clearly ahead

Crucially, order-service shows the SAME storage error independently ("INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device", first at 15:00:42Z), so this is a shared-storage/blast-radius event, not specific to the payment v6.0.0 mandate flow. ledgers-db's own write failures are internal storage exhaustion (out of disk for WAL/data files), not a downstream dependency failure of ledger-db.

critiques.summary: H1 (ledger-db storage exhaustion from retained WAL) is the only hypothesis consistent with the full evidence set. Temporal order is decisive: ledger-db's disk-pressure WARNs start 13:10Z and WAL-retention warnings at 13:02Z (F9) — ~1.5h BEFORE the only change in the window, payment-service v6.0.0 at 14:46Z (F1/F13) — and the consumers fail at 15:00:26Z/15:00:42Z. Scope is explained by the shared postgres: order-service (no change received, never writes MANDATE_HOLD) fails independently with the identical 'No space left on device' error (F11/F16), which a payment-code-path bug or an enum/type rejection (H3) cannot produce. Mechanism is grounded in ledger-db's own internal PANICs writing pg_wal and data files (F10), and the dominant client error (354x) is a storage error, not a type/constraint error (F8). H2 is properly demoted: its central hop (extra write volume from MANDATE_HOLD) has no supporting metric (automated check), and its timeline is impossible — the volume was already 90% at 13:10Z and only reached 98% at 14:48Z, far too slow a trajectory to be launched by a 14:46Z deploy, and F7 shows error rate stayed 59-64% well past the 15:12Z rollback. Accepted, with confidence capped below the stated 0.82 because the disk-fill trajectory is log-derived only (no independent ledger-db disk_used_pct metric) and the inactive-replication-slot mechanism is an inferred, unread assumption. Remaining open questions are confirmatory of an already-established origin, not discriminators between competing origins, so no further round is warranted.

challenges.issue: The quantitative disk trajectory (90%@13:10Z -> 95%@14:15Z -> 98%@14:48Z) rests entirely on log WARN lines (F9); no independent ledger-db disk_used_pct metric was queried. The whole 'disk was already filling before the deploy' grounding therefore has no metric corroboration.

The causal chain implies the DB PANIC (15:01:01Z) precedes client failures, but payment-service (15:00:26Z) and order-service (15:00:42Z) errored BEFORE the DB's own PANIC (F12). Ordering is explainable but as written the chain is internally inconsistent; state that clients began failing as the volume became effectively full, not after the PANIC.
The inactive-replication-slot / retained-WAL mechanism is inferred from matching log wording against HIST-114; the slot's identity was never read. It is an explicit unread assumption, not verified.

H2's pivotal hop (v6.0.0 mandate flow measuredly increased ledger-db write volume) has zero supporting evidence and is flagged by the automated check; it is correctly ranked low but its stated confidence (0.22) still overstates the case given the pre-deploy fill timeline.

H4 names no distinct origin — it converges on ledger-db resource exhaustion and is really a verification frame around the rollback intervention. Presenting it as a separate ranked hypothesis is redundant and slightly inflates apparent uncertainty between origins.
